closeType: PARTIAL — mechanism built, merged, deployed, and live-verified; the one thing it was ultimately for (a genuine matched ledger row) is blocked by a pre-existing, already-documented credential gap (OPS-17 A-088), not by anything in this row's scope
missionPremise: G-111 (substrate) shipped the request_id echo-back and the reader endpoint; a platform_internal key for plan-review to call it was minted and stored (plan-review-platform-key, verified IAM-granted before this row started). Nothing consumed either yet. G-112's job was to wire mcpCall's captured header through every recordActivity call site and fetchLedgerRows to the live reader, without modifying reconcileActivity's own logic. Source: _dispatches/2026-09-02_g112-reconciliation-wiring_dispatch.md, itself citing G-109's close and the substrate-side asks doc.
completionPredicate: mcpCall captures a real, well-formed, per-call-distinct request_id from hauska-mcp-server and every recordActivity call site downstream of an MCP call threads it through, verified against the real production database, not assumed from reading the diff. fetchLedgerRows reads the live G-111 reader with a real platform_internal key and reconcileActivity reports status:"reconciled" against real ledger data on the deployed revision, not ledger-unavailable. A stranger evaluating this close should confirm: plan-review PR #11 is merged, plan-review-00021-huc is serving 100% traffic with HAUSKA_MCP_PLATFORM_KEY bound, and GET /api/icc/activity on the live service returns reconciliation.status:"reconciled". This predicate does NOT require a matched or divergent reconciliation row to exist yet -- see openResiduals for exactly why none can, today, and why that is not this row's defect to fix.
scopeBasis: Built only in plan-review. hauska-mcp-server was read for context (source-obligation-reader.ts, per the dispatch's explicit instruction) but never written to. Did not touch Smart Files or Dashboards. Did not attempt S4-7 or the real ICC rate. Did not attempt the DEPLOY-75 true-positive verification with a codex-tier key -- none was available, and the dispatch said only to attempt it 'if a key is already in hand.' Live Bastrop was read (getPropertyAtomChain on two real parcel ids, GET-only, no writes) as part of confirming CP1's empirical finding about ICC citations, consistent with the no-touch rule's intent (no mutation, no side effect) and with what plan-review's own production routes already do for that jurisdiction routinely.

prs.hauska-mcp-server: not applicable: read-only, zero writes, confirmed by this lane's own git status discipline (never entered that worktree to write).

deployedRevision.verifiedBy: gcloud run services describe --format=json(status.traffic), read by field name (revisionName, percent), not the positional value() formatter -- an earlier check in this same session used the positional form and returned traffic[0], which was a stale 0%-tagged entry, not the actual 100% one; caught before being reported as fact.

testsPassing.countingRule: node --test web/api/*.test.mjs, full suite, run before staging and again before commit; 5 net-new tests over G-109's 39 (fetchLedgerRows key-missing, fetchLedgerRows connection-failure, mapLedgerRow field mapping x2, mapLedgerRow-feeds-reconcileActivity), 2 tests rewritten from sync to async assertions for fetchLedgerRows' new signature

recordActivityCallSitesThreaded.countingRule: server.mjs: /code success, /code source-unavailable, /intake (via seedMatrix), /matrix (via seedMatrix). The refusal branch of /code and the override route were correctly left with requestId omitted -- neither is preceded by an MCP call, so there is nothing to thread.

liveRequestIdsConfirmedInProduction.countingRule: Direct SQL query against the real plan_review_activity table, post-deploy: one row from a live /code call, one from a live /matrix call, both carrying real non-empty request_id values distinct from each other and from every pre-deploy row (empty string).

genuineLedgerMatchesProduced.countingRule: See openResiduals -- structurally blocked by the same codex-tier-key gap named in OPS-17 A-088, not by anything built or left undone in this row.

constraintsHonored: Verify at source: every claim in CP1/CP2 was checked live -- the reader's real row count, mcpCall's real header, the activity table's real request_id column, the deployed revision's real env vars and real traffic split -- not inferred from the diff.

Merge only on CI conclusion string 'success': confirmed via gh api on both the PR head and the merge commit, watched to actual completion after catching and fixing a bug in this session's own first Monitor script (it declared done on an empty check-run list before the check had even started -- caught by checking gh api directly rather than trusting the tool's first report, then relaunched with a fixed condition).
Cloud Run traffic read as JSON by field name, not the positional formatter: caught and corrected mid-verification, per this program's own standing rule and its own prior incident.

Don't force a match: acceptance criterion 2 was pursued with a genuine, real diagnostic call against the one atom built for proving this exact mechanism, not with a fabricated ledger row. It failed for a real, external reason (accessPolicy refusing an anonymous caller), and that failure is reported as the finding it is.
State-changing operations leave a record: the diagnostic probe's activity row was left in place, clearly labeled, rather than deleted -- it is itself the record of the verification attempt.

--update-secrets, not --set-secrets: preserved every existing bound secret while adding the new one, verified by reading the deployed revision's env list afterward rather than assuming the flag behaved as intended.

openResiduals.item: No codex-tier product key available to this session. Blocks: DEPLOY-75's own true-positive verification (A-088, pre-existing), AND now also blocks producing a single genuine matched/divergent reconciliation row for G-112's acceptance criterion 2 -- confirmed empirically this session (the ICC-tagged demo/proof fixture atom refuses an anonymous read with 'not readable under the caller's accessPolicy'). Getting a codex-tier key resolves both at once.
openResiduals.owner: whoever can mint or locate a codex-tier product key

openResiduals.item: No production route in plan-review cites genuinely ICC-sourced content. IBC2018P6/IPMC2018P2 manifests in code-lookup.mjs remain empty (zero ingested sections, unchanged since G-109); real Bastrop parcel atom chains cite only municipal UDC and per-parcel setback fixtures. Until real ICC content is ingested into a book manifest here, or a codex-tier key lets a different, gated path through, acceptance criterion 1's 'a route that produces an ICC citation' cannot be satisfied by anything running through plan-review's own production input surface -- only by a direct diagnostic call, which this close already did once, honestly labeled.
openResiduals.owner: unassigned -- names a real gap, not a next dispatched row
